"SafeRec evidence package, session %2$s
Recording started: %1$s

What is inside
- merged.mp4: the whole recording in one video, to watch. It is put together from the chunks below: the chunks are the evidence.
- evidence/: the session's files exactly as they were uploaded to Google Drive while recording:
 - video chunks (.mp4), about 10 seconds each;
 - their RFC 3161 timestamps (.tsa), issued by Sectigo, a public Time Stamping Authority: each proves its chunk existed, unchanged, at that time;
 - for a chunk repaired after a crash or a power cut, the untouched original (.cut) and its timestamp (.cut.tsa);
 - the session manifest (.manifest), listing every chunk with its SHA-256 fingerprint, and its timestamp (.manifest.tsa).
- report.txt: the session at a glance.
- verify_session.py: checks that the evidence is complete and unchanged.

How to check it
1. Install uv (https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and make sure the openssl command is available (it is on Linux and macOS).
2. Unzip this package, open a terminal in its folder and run:
 uv run verify_session.py evidence
3. It ends with COMPLETE when every chunk listed in the manifest is present and unchanged and every timestamp is valid. Otherwise it says NOT VERIFIED, and why.

This phone ran the same checks when it made this package: their result is in report.txt.

Timestamps exist only if timestamping was turned on in the app."
Timestamp times are read from the files. This phone checked the session when it made the package (above): run verify_session.py to check it again.

Auto: a new piece every 10 seconds

SafeRec records video and sound and sends each 10-second piece to your Google Drive as soon as it can. What reached Drive stays safe even if the phone is broken or taken. Without a network it keeps recording, and the pieces wait on the phone.
SafeRec needs them to record, and notifications to show that it is recording.
